study: Public-verifier blind spot in a Copilot cancellation repair
scope: One previously exposed historical cancellation repair, three paired trials, one task cluster. Development challenge only; no unseen confirmation, collaboration or production claim.

method.comparison: Alternating arm order, matched two-attempt ceilings, fresh strong fallback after a rejected draft. All calls finish before full grading. Exact edits apply to the original baseline.
method.context: Both arms receive identical baseline source, unchanged lifecycle helpers and the public suite. Source was previously exposed in this research campaign.
method.qualification: Preserve all baseline tests. Add a public reserve-abort empty-body probe to both suites. The original reserve and observe cancellation regressions remain final-only. The public probe was authored after reading the original regression.
method.verification: Both arms use short-circuit public verification; accepted candidates must pass all 18 public tests and compile. All six candidates passed, so no fallback ran. Final-only full grading checks 20 tests after all model calls.
method.runtime: Existing immutable exact-lock sandbox; no downloads or new compute allocation. Original public and full repository suites plus Worker compilation.
method.cost: Integer microUSD estimates from recorded usage and frozen tariffs, not invoices. Cache-neutral normalization prices all input at the base rate.
method.elapsed: Per-arm elapsed time includes generation and public verification. Separate full grading is excluded from both arms. Two strong candidates hit the 118-second in-container full-suite timeout (exit 137); those failures remain in the quality denominator.
method.gates: Full correctness, zero false accepts and at least 20% savings on both cost measures. Development lead additionally requires a successful fallback rescue and elapsed ratio <=1.2. Thresholds unchanged.
method.limits: Previously exposed source and a regression-informed public probe preclude unseen confirmation. Three repeats of one task do not establish task-level confidence. Private protocols/raw proof are retained by hash; this report is not a standalone reproduction bundle.

decision.accepted: Retain as a verifier blind-spot development result and evidence that the small model can solve this task. Do not promote the routing policy.
decision.reason: Small candidates pass 3/3 full suites; strong candidates pass 1/3 with two timed-out full grades. No fallback rescue occurred. Cost and latency ratios compare arms with unequal successful completion, so they are descriptive only.
decision.productionGate: 30 unseen real tasks with three trials each, task-clustered uncertainty and unchanged quality/cost/latency controls remain required.
decision.deployment: None. No routing default or production configuration changed.

summaryFieldMeaning.falseAccepts: Counts only cascade public acceptances that fail the full suite. See publicFalseAcceptsByArm for both arms.
summaryFieldMeaning.invalidFullGrades: Timeout rows have unknown test counts (-1), not zero failures. They count as unsuccessful candidates.

diagnosis.status: Inference from saved code and failure traces; no counterfactual repair tested.
diagnosis.finding: Both timed-out strong drafts add a disposal promise to the bounded response-producer list. The original list allows three response slots; adding disposal appears to consume the retirement-reply slot. The reference joins disposal through the physical-work promise instead.
diagnosis.implication: An empty aborted response is insufficient evidence of correct cleanup. Public verification needs a bounded complete retirement lifecycle, including successful retirement acknowledgment and release, before accepting this bug class.
